findings.place: description, fact (5) (and the analyst's issue I13); criterion 7
findings.what: Measured on the clone's Pixel Office server (Node 22.23.4): the 16 KiB limit counts the bytes of the header names and values, not the whole head. 500 lines in all with 31-byte values: head 17 490 B (names+values 15 972 B) -> 200; with 32-byte values: 17 988 B (16 470 B) -> 431; 990 lines with 15-byte values: head 18 832 B (15 844 B) -> 200; 300 lines with 60-byte values: 19 132 B -> 431. So «a head over 16 384 bytes is refused by the size limit whatever the count» does not hold, and the example of fact 5 («2 000 lines of 11 bytes, 22 920 bytes → 431») does not separate size from count, because 2 000 lines are over the count limit (1 000 lines in all -> 200, 1 001 -> 431, measured). The bound of criterion 7 («the whole head under 16 384 bytes, so the count refuses it and not the size») is still right as a sufficient bound: under it the size limit cannot act.
findings.needed: The wording and the evidence of fact 5 match the measurement, so that a design does not build a size row on whole-head bytes.
